title: Evaluating and Rewarding LALMs for Expressive Role-Play TTS via Mean Continuation Log-Probability
claim: A pretrained likelihood-based scorer measures style continuity and, combined with a content-fidelity penalty, serves as the RL reward for tuning the generator.
layout: 3 panels: pretraining top, model bottom-left, rewards bottom-right; legend box left
description: A large system diagram split into three labeled panels, with a legend at the upper left. The legend defines colored circles for text tokens, squares for audio tokens, flame and snowflake icons for trainable and frozen modules, and dashed-border colors for the SFT, pretrain and RL stages. Panel (a), top right, shows a long transcription and a long audio input split into interleaved segments (T_s1, TA4_s1, and so on). These feed a wide brown 'LALM For MCLP' block, which outputs token groups. Panel (b), bottom left, shows a blue LALM block that takes scene and characters, role-play instruction and TA4 tokens as input and produces N rollouts. Panel (c), bottom right, has a content reward branch (token2wav, ASR, CER) and a style reward branch (MCLP score from log-probabilities). Both branches feed from a frozen LALM For MCLP block. Dashed lines and orange arrows show the flow.
caption: The overall framework of our proposed method. (a) The pretraining stage of the LALM for computing MCLP. (b) The LALM is fine-tuned to generate interleaved TA4 tokens conditioned on a structured prompt containing scene descriptions, character profiles, and dialogue history. (c) The hybrid reward function for GRPO that synergizes the style-centric MCLP signal with a content-fidelity penalty (CER) to prevent reward hacking.
abstract: Recent advances in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) have extended Text-to-Speech (TTS) to interactive role-play scenarios, which demand high expressiveness and strict adherence to role-play instructions. However, existing models struggle to maintain stylistic consistency with character profiles and scene descriptions across multi-turn dialogues. A critical bottleneck is the lack of objective metrics for quantifying speaking style. To bridge this gap, we propose Mean Continuation Log-Probability (MCLP) as both an evaluation metric and a reward signal, validated on LALM-based Role-Play TTS (RP-TTS) tasks. MCLP leverages the in-context learning capability of pretrained LALMs to measure the likelihood of ground-truth speech tokens conditioned on a contextual history consisting of the transcript, generated speech, and repeated transcript, serving as a proxy for stylistic continuity. Furthermore, we employ MCLP as a reinforcement learning reward to enhance the style alignment between generated speech and role-play instructions. To support this task, we construct a large-scale RP-TTS dataset with rich scene and character annotations. Experiments demonstrate that MCLP is well aligned with human judgments of stylistic consistency and serves as an effective reward for improving RP-TTS, leading to consistent gains in both objective metrics and subjective evaluations. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/y-ren16/MCLP.
